package_info.package_versions: All versions unless patched for all listed CVEs; specifically, versions with DefaultTyping enabled and missing blacklist updates
package_info.why_malicious: The package enables polymorphic deserialization by default (DefaultTyping), which allows attackers to supply malicious serialized objects (gadgets) that can trigger remote code execution (RCE) when deserialized. The core design makes it inherently risky unless strict developer hygiene and explicit type whitelisting are enforced. Multiple CVEs exist due to the evolving blacklist approach, but the fundamental risk persists.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when deserializing untrusted data with DefaultTyping enabled)
execution_context.file_location: Application code using ObjectMapper with DefaultTyping enabled

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This payload leverages Jackson's polymorphic deserialization to instantiate an attacker-controlled class (BaddApp.Obj) with attacker-supplied arguments, potentially triggering a gadget chain that leads to arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The payload explicitly sets the @class property, allowing the attacker to control the type instantiated during deserialization. This is a classic gadget-based deserialization attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal deserialization should only instantiate safe, expected types. Here, arbitrary types can be instantiated based on attacker input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Polymorphic deserialization is legitimate when used with trusted data and a strict type whitelist.
key_indicators: No type whitelist or blacklist enforcement

execution_context.trigger: library initialization (class load time); affects all deserialization operations
required_permissions: none (library code, but enables dangerous behavior)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: public JsonDeserializer<Object> createBeanDeserializer(DeserializationContext ctxt, JavaType type, BeanDescription beanDesc) throws JsonMappingException { ... }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This method is responsible for creating deserializers for arbitrary Java types. When DefaultTyping is enabled, it allows instantiation of attacker-supplied classes if not blacklisted.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The method enables deserialization of arbitrary types, which is dangerous if type information is attacker-controlled.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected behavior is to only deserialize safe, known types. This method allows dynamic type resolution based on input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate for trusted data and explicit type mapping.
key_indicators: Dynamic type resolution based on input
No strict type whitelist by default

execution_context.trigger: library initialization (static block); applies to all deserialization operations
required_permissions: none (library code, but controls deserialization policy)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Defines a blacklist of dangerous classes that should not be deserialized. This is a mitigation to block known gadget classes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The need for a growing blacklist indicates the underlying deserialization mechanism is unsafe by design.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected: only explicitly allowed types can be deserialized. Actual: all types allowed except those blacklisted.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Blacklists are a common mitigation, but not a substitute for whitelisting.

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious JSON payload with @class property pointing to a gadget class.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is submitted to a vulnerable application endpoint.

attack_chain.action: Application deserializes the payload using ObjectMapper with DefaultTyping enabled.
attack_chain.leads_to: Jackson library attempts to instantiate the attacker-supplied class.

attack_chain.action: If the class is not blacklisted, Jackson instantiates the class, triggering the gadget chain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution in the application context.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of JSON with @class property from untrusted sources
Use of ObjectMapper with DefaultTyping enabled
Instantiation of classes not explicitly whitelisted during deserialization
file_indicators: Absence of custom TypeResolverBuilder or explicit type whitelisting
Presence of large or growing blacklists in deserialization config
network_indicators: Inbound requests containing @class in JSON payloads
Unusual outbound connections following deserialization (if RCE is exploited)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan application code for use of ObjectMapper.enableDefaultTyping() or similar APIs. Monitor for inbound JSON payloads containing @class or other type indicators. Audit deserialization logic to ensure only explicitly allowed types are permitted. Review application logs for instantiation of unexpected classes during deserialization. Use runtime instrumentation to detect dynamic class loading from untrusted input.
